svg.text: Why leaders struggle with improvement, and how to break out
Conditions shape beliefs; beliefs drive behaviours; behaviours produce results; results reinforce the conditions. Strategy and capability set the limits.
Why leaders struggle
with improvement
Beliefs
Improving isn’t my job: luck will come along
Idle people are waste: keep everyone busy
If it isn’t broken, don’t fix it
More projects mean more output
Expects quick results: short-term thinking
The problem is the staff, customers or suppliers
I know better
Afraid to look stupid: won’t ask for help
It’s quicker to do it myself
We’ve been fine, or will be fine (complacency)
Conditions
No slack, time or money
Staff keep leaving
Too many inexperienced staff at once
A few people resist any change
No real support from bosses
Fear: problems are not raised
Fixed jobs and departments: silos, own goals
Measures reward busyness and fire-fighting
Clumsy tools; inaccurate or missing information
Strategic position
Wrong market
Wrong products
Wrong organisation
Targets crowd out purpose
Few key people, suppliers, customers, products
Behaviours
Too busy fire-fighting
Relies on quick fixes and workarounds
Too many meetings
Can’t say no: staff, customers, suppliers
Too many priorities: wants it all
Doesn’t delegate or write routines down
Doesn’t listen or ask staff for help
Hires clever people, leaves them to it
No time set aside to improve
Accepts any work, at any price
Too many projects: multitasking kills flow
Waits for a grand solution
Capability and learning
Not learning
Not looking outside the organisation
No improvement method
Doesn’t understand variation and noise
Improves away from the constraint: waste
Imposes one final solution; no experiments
How to break out
Protect improvement time first
answers: No time set aside to improve
Write the routine down; delegate
answers: Quicker to do it myself
Keep a stop-doing list; learn to say no
answers: Too many priorities; can’t say no
Find the constraint; improve there first
answers: Improving away from the constraint
Create slack deliberately; charge the right price
answers: Keep everyone busy; any work at any price
Finish before starting; limit work in progress
answers: Too many projects; multitasking
Quality over speed: fix it properly, even if slower
answers: Quick fixes and workarounds
Change the measures: count flow, prevention, improvement
answers: Measures reward busyness
Reward prevention, not fire-fighting heroics
answers: Fire-fighting gets the credit
Fix the tools and information that force workarounds
answers: Clumsy tools; missing information
Prevention: a stitch in time; ask what could go wrong (FMEA)
answers: If it isn’t broken, don’t fix it
Learn about variation; test for real change
answers: Variation and noise
Run small experiments to find what works for you
answers: One final solution
Think in years; start small, improve step by step
answers: Short-term thinking; waiting for a grand solution
Roles, not job descriptions: flexible teams, shared goals
answers: Fixed jobs and departments; silos
Build resilience: spread the dependence; double bet
answers: Dependence on a few key people, suppliers, customers, products
Ask for help, information or directions: a strength
answers: Afraid to look stupid
Look at how the work is done, not the people
answers: Blaming staff, customers or suppliers
Ask staff; go and see; make it safe to speak up
answers: I know better; fear
Learn from others: bright spots, others’ incidents
answers: Not looking outside
Luck = capability + opportunity: build capability
answers: Luck will come along
